text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti, marking a year since his government was formed, says his cabinet achieved tangible results in all spheres.
- Education minister denies that the ministry is about to change school syllabus; says this is the prerogative of the higher education council, which is yet to be formed.
- 412 million dinars ($582 million) is the estimated cost of road projects in the kingdom in the next few years.
- Palestinian leader Faisal al-Husseini asks Jordan to stop Israeli plans in Jersalem.
- Islamist figure Abdullah Akaylah says that the government has not raised with the Islamists the proposal for them to join the cabinet after a reshuffle.
- Amounts embezzeled in the doctors union are more than the published figures; three employees taken to court.
- Jordanian figures join in the "Arab-Israeli coalition for peace" set up in an informal meeting in Denmark.
- Crown prince stresses need for coordination and focus in developing sports movement.
